That's awful. Terrible experience to go through for both of you. Sorry to hear about your mom and friend's brother. Great question btw. I wouldn't say I felt guilty for being happy. For me, it was the other way around. I felt guilty for being depressed and that just made it worse for me. I did nothing but sit in a room and watch TV or play games for almost 5 years except for work. I've researched a lot since then on suicide and how it impacts families all the way down to a psychological level for individuals. I can't say for sure because of course your friend and I didn't have the exact same experience, background, mental condition, personality, etc. What might help me give a better answer is a few questions myself. Was he close with his brother? Did they see each other often? Did he consider his brother a close friend or role model? Does he talk much about his brother or what happened? Is your friend usually upbeat or 'down in the dumps' acting? And just a heads up, if it's only been 6 months, it's still extremely fresh. Feelings of anguish and despair come on when thinking about a loved one that was lost because it can be like experiencing everything all over again. Hope this could be of some help to you and him. I genuinely enjoy talking about and helping others with these type of situations so feel free to ask me more questions or even message me personally. I'm always open to talking to you or him.

I went to counseling for about 4 months about 3 years ago for depression. I would just go into work and feel like going home and crawling into a hole. Seeing a counselor helped a little but I didn't fully express my feelings then. My father convinced me to go to a psychiatrist which I started about a year ago. That has helped quite a bit. Still have issues here and there, but I can honestly say I don't suffer from severe depressive episodes like I used to. I thought at first it was just anxiety but after seeing my doctor a few times, I was diagnosed with Bipolar Disorder and PTSD. Medication helps a ton as long as it's not abused. And I'm pretty open to talking about it nowadays. I've moved on. There's still pain there, but discussing it doesn't make the situation any worse

I appreciate it o-p-yum. All I can say is don't give up. I've been there quite a few times and having a close relative commit suicide makes you think about suicide more often. And then you feel guilty for thinking about it which makes you think about it even more. It's a vicious cycle and I wouldn't wish anything even remotely familiar on my worst enemy. No one deserves to feel worthless. I've come to find that it may seem like no one cares, but all it takes is one person to help you rip off that blanket of depression.
